name: LocalizationJson
src_typeComment: Reads and writes the other shape translations arrive in: ONE FILE PER LANGUAGE, a flat object of key -> text.  { "ui.start": "Start", "ui.quit": "Quit" }  Nested objects are flattened with dots, so the equally common  { "ui": { "start": "Start", "quit": "Quit" } }  produces exactly the same keys — which is what makes a file exported from a web translation tool drop straight in.  WHY THIS EXISTS RATHER THAN JsonHelper: a localisation file is a string -> string map and nothing else, and JsonUtility cannot deserialize a Dictionary at all. The toolkit's JsonHelper can, but it needs the Newtonsoft package, and the convention here is that a tool does not drag a package in for one narrow job — the same reasoning that produced CsvUtility instead of a spreadsheet library. If your file has numbers, arrays or nested non-string values, it is not a localisation file: use JsonHelper for it.

src_members.comment: Always written flat, one key per line, sorted — a localisation file lives in source control and gets re-exported constantly, so a stable line order is what keeps its diffs readable.
